question: Where will the great white shark Percy be on November 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Latest Ocearch ping (2026-08-11, 44.88N 62.07W) is off Nova Scotia's Eastern Shore, so Nova Scotia is due west; there has been no ping for 61 days and 21 days remain. Percy pings sparsely (57 pings in ~14 months, previous gaps of 45 and 49 days; last fall he went silent from Oct 4 to Nov 22). I estimate ~35% chance of a new ping before Nov 1. If one comes, he will be migrating south in autumn: maybe a third chance he is still off Nova Scotia, the rest spread across Gulf of Maine/MA/NY/NJ/south. I found no human prediction market on this; the harness's Manifold candidate (great white extinction) does not match.
calls.dossier:

- Event window: whatever ping is latest at 2026-11-01. As of 2026-10-11 there are about 21 days left for a new ping to land.
- Percy: sub-adult male, 9'9", 432 lb, tagged 2025-07-28 in Mahone Bay, Nova Scotia (Fox Weather, Aug 2026).
- Latest ping per the Mapotic/Ocearch API, fetched 2026-10-11: 2026-08-11 01:12 UTC at 44.88N, 62.07W (off the Eastern Shore of Nova Scotia; mainland Nova Scotia is due west). Before that: 2026-08-09 at 44.77N 61.42W; 2026-08-03 at 42.93N 65.41W (south of Nova Scotia; due west at that latitude is roughly the NH/MA coast); 2026-07-28 at about 40.0-40.46N 73-73.5W (off Long Island/NJ); 2026-07-22/23 at about 36.0-36.5N 75.1-75.2W (off NC/VA).
- Status quo: no ping since Aug 11 (61 days of silence as of Oct 11). If nothing new arrives, the answer stays Nova Scotia.
- Ping frequency: 57 pings in about 14.5 months, in clusters. Gaps over 30 days: Aug 1 to Sep 15, 2025 (45 days) and Oct 4 to Nov 22, 2025 (49 days). The current 61-day gap is the longest on record; could be tag degradation or just not surfacing.
- Autumn 2025 path: Sep 15 and Oct 4, 2025 at about 44.0-44.1N 66.3W (Bay of Fundy mouth / Grand Manan area; due west is Maine); then Nov 22-23, 2025 at 39.0-39.8N 72-73.6W (off NJ); Nov 25 at 37.7N 75.4W (off VA). After that he wintered as far south as the Gulf of Mexico.
- Latitude bands for due west: Long Island about 40.55-41.1N (New York); NJ coast about 38.93-40.5N; MA (Cape Cod/islands) about 41.2-42.85N; NH coast about 42.87-43.08N (not an option, so 'Anywhere else'); Maine about 43.08-44.8N; Nova Scotia for pings east of about 66W at about 43.4-45.5N.
- Markets: searched for Percy-specific markets, none found. The harness's Manifold candidate (great white extinction by 2099) is unrelated.
- Searched for but not found: any news of Percy pings after August 2026, or Ocearch statements on his tag's health.
calls.reference_class: Percy's own ping record: the chance a 3-week window brings a new ping, given his sparse ping clusters and 45-49 day gaps, plus where he was last autumn (Bay of Fundy in early Oct, off NJ/Delmarva in late Nov 2025)

calls.reasoning: Status quo dominates: the last ping (2026-08-11, 44.88N 62.07W) has mainland Nova Scotia due west, and no ping has come in 61 days, his longest gap on record. With ~21 days left I put a new ping at ~28%, lower than the runs' 30-35% because a gap this long hints at tag degradation. If he pings, the last-autumn analog (Gulf of Maine/Bay of Fundy mouth in Sep-Oct, off NJ by late Nov) puts most of that mass on NS/Maine, with a tail spread south. No human market exists.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the last ping is 2026-08-11 off eastern NS with NS due west, there have been no Sep/Oct pings, the autumn-2025 pattern is the same in each dossier, and no matching market exists. The only factual loose end is an Aug 16 Z-ping with no coordinates. I could not check it without web access, and it would most likely also be in NS waters, so it barely matters. The remaining disagreements are judgment calls: the chance of a ping in the next 21 days, and where he would be if one arrives. I took a slightly lower ping chance (~28%) because the current gap exceeds every previous one, and I weighted any October ping toward NS and the Gulf of Maine, matching last October's positions. Reference class carried forward from the runs.
